validation: 500 boards pass Python and TypeScript gates and solve in the game engine. Only copied later wheel-size checks changed; every other source check matches production. Negative tests reject eight tiles before level 346, nine tiles, and 74-level required-variant gaps; 75 is accepted. Deterministic rebuild verified. Actual wheel layout/hit-test geometry passes at 245–300 pt. Production reviewed-only loader rejects draft.
method: Keep first 345 required boards; allow 7 or 8 tiles at levels 346–500. Retain the prior seven-tile candidate pool and add source-approved eight-tile boards. Use the same variety-oriented ranking, objective weights, stop selection, pacing and shape checks. Preserve the same maximum five shared tiles with any preceding ten-level wheel, generalized to eight-tile candidates without weakening the threshold.
limitations: Bounded candidate search, per-stop selection and fixed first 345 boards; not a global optimum or a pure exhaustive comparison of all possible seven/eight-tile layouts. Geometry is not device playtesting. Eight-tile wheels add potential combinations and raise the existing heuristic difficulty by eight points for otherwise identical answers. No new destinations, artwork, production dictionary, live campaign or app export.
